newsitem.title: USA: D'Amato wants Swiss bank guard to stay in U.S.
newsitem.headline: D'Amato wants Swiss bank guard to stay in U.S.

text.p: New York Republican Sen. Alfonse D'Amato introduced legislation on Wednesday to give permanent U.S. resident status to Swiss bank guard Christophe Meili, calling him a "righteous man without a country."

The ex-Union Bank guard was denounced in Switzerland after he alerted authorities to the destruction of Holocaust-era bank records. He was fired from the security firm and he and his family have received death threats.

At a recent hearing of the Senate Banking Committee, which D'Amato heads, Mieli said: "Please protect me in the U.S.A. and in Switzerland. I think I have become a great problem in Switzerland. I have a (wife), two little children and no future."

"He should be given his opportunity," D'Amato told Reuters. "He is truly a person who has demonstrated great courage. He thought he was doing something right and was ostracized and threatened with death. He is a righteous man now without a country."
Six U.S. senators have joined D'Amato in co-sponsoring legislation to allow the Mieli family to become permanent residents and hearings will be held next week.
